extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and administrative staff preparing NIH-style biographical sketches and budget justifications for grant applications (senior/key personnel and other significant contributors).
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and content expectations for Senior/Key Personnel biographical sketches and the personnel sections of a grant budget justification: what fields to include, page limits, how to present education, positions, contributions to science, research support, and personnel effort/roles in budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch overall format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified format for each person and keep the entire biographical sketch to five pages or fewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each entry include institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study. Start with the baccalaureate and include subsequent training; add or delete rows to reflect the individual's training history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize relevant experience, expertise, and how the individual will contribute to the proposed project. Include years of experience, major accomplishments, relevant technical skills, prior roles on related projects, and explicit ties to the current application aims (examples in the document illustrate describing specific expertise and planned contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: B. POSITIONS AND HONORS -- Positions and Employment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List professional positions and employment history (dates and titles). Include other experience and professional memberships, and list honors. Present positions in chronological order with dates; include significant leadership or relevant institutional roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe up to several major contributions (numbered) to science with a brief narrative of the contribution and 3–4 representative publications or citations per contribution. Each contribution should explain significance, context, and the applicant's role. Provide selected citations (journal, year, volume, pages) beneath each contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete list of published work link
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete List of Published Work in MyBibliography: [URL]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a URL to the applicant's complete MyBibliography (NCBI link) for a full publication list, in addition to the selected citations included in Contributions to Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support (current and prior)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. RESEARCH SUPPORT -- Current and Previous: list grant number, project title, sponsor, role, dates, and brief project description and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each support entry specify project period (dates), funding source (e.g., NIH institute or other agency), the applicant's role (Investigator, PI, Subaward PI, Key Personnel), a concise description of the project's aims and the applicant's contributions or responsibilities, and indicate overlap statements (e.g., 'Overlap – none'). Include both ongoing and completed support with explicit dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed Research Support entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed Research Support: list prior grants with title, sponsor, role, dates, and brief outcomes/aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what the project determined or produced (e.g., 'This project determined the impact of malaria on EBOV infection and defined the roles of specific cytokines...'), the role the individual had (e.g., Subaward PI), and the project period. Use concise outcome-focused language for completed grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification: personnel identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel section should list each named person with title, role (e.g., Key Personnel), and planned effort (calendar months or percent effort) across project years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each person include name, degree/title, institutional affiliation, role on project (e.g., Project Leader, Director of Biology), and explicit time commitment (e.g., 'Yrs 1-3: 3 cal. months' or '0.6 cal. months'). Use consistent units (calendar months per year) and clearly state which years the effort applies to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification: responsibilities and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: For each personnel entry, provide a concise justification describing the individual's specific responsibilities on the project and relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what the person will do (e.g., 'will be responsible for FCCDC project design, direction of the project and data interpretation', 'will perform computer-assisted drug design studies', 'will conduct cytotoxicity assays at FCCDC in liver HepG2 and endothelial HUVEC'). Mention relevant prior experience or accomplishments that justify the role and time requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification: safety, confidentiality, and data practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Include commitments around laboratory safety, confidentiality, productivity, notebook keeping and spectral data records retention for personnel conducting experimental work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing bench personnel justify that work will be performed under appropriate safety and data-management practices and note expectations for recordkeeping and data retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification: role in commercialization/transition
rubrics_metrics.description: For senior leadership personnel include planned activities related to transition beyond Phase II and commercialization efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe tasks such as developing commercialization plans, interfacing with development partners, and leveraging regulatory or incentive programs (example: 'seek to ensure a successful transition at the end of Phase II... taking advantage of initiatives such as the Neglected Disease Priority Review Voucher program').
